$comment: Claude Code runtime settings for Alan. The prompt is portable/claude-code/agents/alan.md; this file is the config that has no business inside a prompt. Read agents/alan/PORTING.md before wiring it up.
$routeComment: general, unlike the other agents here. The work is small, careful edits to existing prose in a voice he has to match, plus the judgment of when feedback is an undecided question rather than a rule — worth more than the fast route, and less than a builder or a reviewer, where confident wrong output is expensive. Move him to reasoning if he starts writing rule text of his own rather than carrying the evidence he was given into it. An agent never names a model: the route names a role, and the stack's site.json maps it to a model. The Claude Code artifact says `model: inherit`, so a session's own model decides there.
$toolsComment: Write and Edit are present, unlike Barb, because editing the skills IS his work — the two agents are deliberate opposites and neither tool list should drift toward the other. No Task: he dispatches nobody. What keeps him safe is not the absence of a write tool but the absence of a merge: he writes to a branch in his own checkout and a person decides. Narrow Bash to git, npm and the forge API if your setup allows; he needs nothing else. npm is also how he finds an adapter's issue tracker (`npm view <package> bugs.url`).
$mergeComment: There is no configuration here that prevents a merge, and there cannot be — a merge is a forge permission, not a tool. Give his credential write access to contents, pull requests and issues on the knowledge repository, issues on the adapter repositories and Theme Forge, and nothing more. The prompt says he never merges; the token is what makes that true.
